findings.description: `rewardTokens` is deliberately NOT deduped (§4.5). A duplicate entry `[T, T]` snapshots the SAME pre-loop balance B twice, and both entries are paid out after the mint loop. The contract's own claim that the second transfer 'fails closed' is FALSE in the live configuration: the dispatcher donates reward token into this contract on EVERY mint (BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch -> ISkyPSM.buyGem(batchMinter, gemAmt) delivers USDC straight to this contract), so the post-loop balance is B + D where D is THIS batch's own donations. The second transfer therefore succeeds whenever D >= B, paying the batcher their own batch's donations. That is exactly the self-funded round-trip that the §4.2 pre-loop snapshot exists to prevent and that the code calls 'load-bearing'. Repeating the token k times extracts k*B while the balance allows, and can drain the entire post-loop balance so that nothing is seeded forward for the next claimant.
missingMitigations: No dedupe of rewardTokens (explicitly declined as O(n^2))
No re-check that the cumulative payout for a token does not exceed its pre-loop snapshot
findings.notes: Cheapest fix that keeps O(n): zero out `snapshot[j]` for any j whose token equals an already-paid token during the payout pass would still be O(n^2); alternatively cap the total transferred per token at the pre-loop balance by tracking a running `paidSoFar` against the snapshot, or simply assert post-loop that `balanceOf(this) >= D` was not consumed. Escalation check for the severity tier: the loss is the NEXT claimant's seed plus a rebate of the batcher's own donation, and it is repeatable.
findings.contradictedDocumentation: docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.5 ('the second either reverts on insufficient balance or transfers into a now-empty pot'); NatSpec on batchMint ('the second transfer fails closed')

findings.description: Step 10 sweeps the ENTIRE residual payment-token balance to `msg.sender` with NO `nudgeSize` gate and no `qualifies` check. The payment token is DERIVED from `dispatcherIndex` at call time and `setDispatcherIndex` is owner-settable at any moment with no compatibility check against the contract's funding sources. If `dispatcherIndex` ever resolves to a dispatcher whose `primeToken()` is also one of this contract's funding tokens, the entire pot becomes (a) unclaimable through the nudge path, because the §4.1 exclusion reverts on listing it as a reward token, and (b) claimable in full by ANY caller with `count == 1`, through the ungated sweep. The concrete instantiation is live in the sibling repo: `NudgeRatchet.primeToken()` is USDC (6-decimal deploy guard) and `NudgeRatchet._dispatch` sweeps its full USDC balance to `batchMinter`, while `DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol` documents the PRIMARY funding path as a 30% USDC drip (`StableYieldAccumulator.setNudgeAddress(<this>)`) into this same contract. Under the intended `DISPATCHER_INDEX = 4` (BalancerPoolerV2, prime token USDS) the configuration is safe; a repoint to the ratchet index inverts it. The deploy script's `require`s check only that `DISPATCHER_INDEX != 0` and the story-022 change explicitly REMOVED the old deploy-time 'nudge token == payment token' guard, replacing it with a per-call revert that protects only the nudge path and does nothing about the sweep path.
missingMitigations: Sweep is not bounded by the caller's own unspent `paymentAmount` (it sweeps third-party/dripped balances too)
No invariant tying `dispatcherIndex`'s primeToken to the set of funding tokens
Deploy-time collision guard was removed, and the replacement per-call guard does not cover the sweep
`setDispatcherIndex` has no re-validation of the funding configuration
findings.notes: Law 3 footgun test: a competent, non-malicious owner repointing `dispatcherIndex` to the USDC-primed NudgeRatchet would be SURPRISED that the nudge pot becomes both unclaimable and free-for-all, and that (if this contract is also the ratchet's `batchMinter`) mint payments round-trip back into this contract and are refunded by the same sweep, making batched mints effectively free while mint-debt still accrues. In-scope hazard, not owner-malice. Even in the safe USDS configuration the sweep hands any stranded/donated payment token to the first `count == 1` caller with no gate; that narrower reading is documented ('a griefer who pre-deposits payment-token simply donates to the next caller') and is parked at MR-BNM-08.

findings.function: stake / unstake / claim / emergencyWithdraw vs poolState
findings.description: `stake` (617), `unstake` (645), `claim` (666) and `emergencyWithdraw` (735) carry no `poolState` gate, so they stay open while the pool is `Migrating`. Two consequences specific to the PRICE-SCALED model, where `R = totalStaked * latestPrice * targetAPY / SECONDS_PER_YEAR` depends on `totalStaked`: (1) a permissionless `stake(1)` during `Migrating` re-populates `totalStaked` while the tail `_recomputeScheduleIfActive()` deliberately no-ops, so the frozen snapshot's `rewardRate` no longer corresponds to the live pool, and any caller can indefinitely block `finalizeAndReset` (which requires `totalStaked == 0`) for one ERC1155 unit; (2) an unstake/emergencyWithdraw during `Migrating` shrinks `totalStaked` without re-sizing R for the same reason. Accrual itself is safe (`_updatePool` early-returns while `Migrating`), so this is availability/state-consistency rather than over-emission.
missingMitigations: No auto-pause on `initiateMigration` (the freeze relies on the operator separately pausing)
`finalizeAndReset`'s `totalStaked == 0` precondition is griefable by any staker
findings.priorArt: Recurrence of ledger entry L-03 (open, Low) 'stake/unstake/claim not poolState-gated during Migrating (no auto-pause) - asymm...' filed against src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol in run-18. NEW CONTRACT, so it mints a new fingerprint and dedup will not link it automatically. The price-scaled variant is materially different from the depletion variant because R depends on totalStaked here, per the contract's own 'PRICE-SCALED DELTA 6a' note.

findings.description: Three caller-controlled unbounded loops: `count` iterations of `nftMinter.mint` (line 363), and two passes over the caller-supplied `rewardTokens` array (424, 454). No cap on `count` and no cap on `rewardTokens.length`; the only bound is the block gas limit. All gas is paid by the caller and the failure mode is self-DoS, so the impact is confined. Recorded because story-022 ADDED a second and third caller-sized loop to a function that already carried an open finding for the first.
findings.priorArt: Ledger L-02 (submitted, Low) 'Uncapped count loop in batchMint'. The rewardTokens loops are new surface on the same root cause.

findings.description: The payout amount is a balance SNAPSHOT taken before the mint loop and transferred verbatim afterwards; `minRewards` is a floor on the contract's pre-transfer balance, not on what `recipient` actually receives. Two skews follow. (a) Fee-on-transfer: the delivered amount is below the declared floor, so `minRewards` does not do what a caller reading it as slippage protection would assume - explicitly documented as caller-discretion. (b) NEGATIVE-REBASING or otherwise shrinking token: if the balance falls between the snapshot and the payout, `safeTransfer(snapshot[i])` reverts and the WHOLE batch (all mints, all other reward tokens) rolls back - a one-token DoS on the entire batch. The token set here is fully permissionless, which is exactly the condition under which this pattern's `notVulnerableWhen` ('token set restricted to known non-fee, non-rebasing tokens') does not hold; the mitigating factor is that the caller selects the tokens and only harms themselves.
missingMitigations: No balanceAfter - balanceBefore measurement on the payout leg
Snapshot amount is not clamped to `min(snapshot[i], currentBalance)` at payout time
findings.notes: Clamping the payout to `min(snapshot[i], balanceOf(this))` would also close PATTERN-001's second-transfer window and remove this revert-DoS in one change. Note the two findings pull in the same direction, so a fix should be evaluated jointly.
